newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends with pared gains after stocks fall.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends with pared gains after stocks fall.

text.p: Copper prices rose on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Friday in response to another sizeable drawdown in stocks, but finished the afternoon kerb session off the day's highs.
Other base metals also finished in the plus column in what was mainly routine trade.
Benchmark three month copper futures ended the kerb at $1,911 a tonne, up $15 from Thursday's close but $7 below the day's high.
LME stocks fell 9,925 tonnes on Friday taking the total down to 229,575 tonnes compared with an early September total of 275,275 tonnes.
Based on continued strong demand for LME warrants, traders expected the drawdown to go on for a few more weeks.
"We're still getting good warrant demand. I expect a few more bullish returns," said one trader.
The price reaction to the big declines recently has been more muted than some traders and analysts expected, but some said bank selling could still be capping the market.
Spreads firmed with prices on Friday. Cash moved out to a $5/8 premium over three month values from level on Thursday.
Dealers attributed the stock declines to shipments from Europe to China and cautious stock rebuilding by consumers and merchants now that steep backwardations are out of the market.
Prices could rally to $1,950 if resistance at $1,920 was broken soon, chartists said. First big support was pegged at $1,880.
Aluminium prices gained ground in sympathy with copper, shrugging off a rise in stocks of 8,550 tonnes.
Prices finished the afternoon kerb $5 higher at $1,357. The market traded in a narrow $4 range all day.
Technical analysts said the market was oversold and due a bounce towards $1,380 resistance soon. Key support was expected to emerge at $1,340, Thursday's 2-1/4 year low.
Nickel prices gained $70 to $7,170, boosted by a 306-tonne fall in stocks and news early in the day of an ongoing production stoppage at the WMC Rocky Reward mine in Australia.
Zinc nudged higher to $1,023 from $1,018.50 after stocks rose 325 tonnes. Lead rose $7 to $771 after stocks fell 250 tonnes.
Tin gained $75 to $6,095 after a stock decline of 95 tonne.
Alloy was last quoted at $1,210/15 from $1,208/10. Stocks fell 980 tonnes.
